note: Every launch that exists on chain, on any chain, and what each one is. Read from the factories rather than remembered. allProjects is append-only with no delete, so this list can only grow -- which is exactly why it is written down once here instead of being re-explained every time totalProjectsCount() is read. audit_consistency.mjs sums totalProjectsCount() across every chain and both factory generations, and fails only when an on-chain launch is NOT accounted for here. chainId is per entry: this file stopped being single-chain when $CURB launched on Monad, and a top-level chainId would have quietly labelled that launch 0G.

The first launch on Monad, built for the Monad Metropolis hackathon and replaced by $PARCEL, which was recorded through the production UI instead of a local build. Its registry row was pulled once $PARCEL succeeded; the backup on the VPS is projects.json.before-curb-removal. So it is no longer listed on the site, but nothing was taken from it: the curve still holds its reserves, the market is still tradable directly against the curve, and the ticker stays claimed on this factory forever because symbolRegistry has no release function. Read from chain at the time it was delisted: symbol CURB, name Curb Market, supply 1e9, agentBound true with agentId 10251, virtualNative 173559.28438 MON, swapCount 5.

The live $PARCEL market, launched through the production UI at adexto.xyz rather than a local build, which is why it appears in the production registry -- see the demo recording procedure. Second launch on Monad. Listed at /token/parcel?chain=143. ERC-8004 agent bound at creation: agentId 10251, checked by the factory against AGENT_REGISTRY 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432 before it would mint. Read from chain: symbol PARCEL, name Parcel Market, supply 1e9, agentBound true, virtualNative 174888.464882 MON, swapCount 5, creator fees accrued and claimed to zero during the run. A parcel is a bounded lot a city is divided into and sold whole, which is the same shape as a curve position: one defined unit, priced as a whole, with no deposit to enter it.
First market on Base. Meme category, opened to give the factory a live market on every mainnet it is deployed to. Launch metadata anchored to 0G DA.

First market on Arbitrum One. Its registration was recovered by hand: the launch broadcast succeeded but the RPC refused the receipt lookup, so the txHash and attestation root were read back from the TrinityProjectDeployed event rather than regenerated.

Launched on camera for the 0G Atlas Founder House demo recording, on 0G mainnet so the same market could then be bought by an external agent over x402 -- the gateway resolves through the production registry, so a local-only launch could not have been bought. Five manual swaps from the web UI, then one buy from the x402 relayer at block 44560323.

The first market from the 0.12.0 factory, opened so the published AdextoCurve ABI could be verified against a curve that generation actually produces. No 0.11.0 market can ever do that: the 0.12.0 curve adds BUYBACK_COOLDOWN() and lastBuybackAt() -- finding 1 of GHSA-g589-wjqq-86f2 -- and every curve is immutable, so the older ones will never carry them. export-abi.mjs refuses to publish an ABI it has not matched against a live instance, which blocked the whole site deploy until this existed. DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED in the site registry: deployTrinity was called directly rather than through /api/deploy, so metadataRoot is bytes32(0), nothing is anchored to 0G DA, and the market does not appear in the explorer, the x402 gateway or the MCP tools -- all three read the registry. Monad was chosen because it is the cheapest of the four: 3,249,106 gas at 102 gwei, about 0.66 MON. Fee legs confirmed on chain as the 0.12.0 model: depth 10 / creator 70 / buyback 10 / protocol 10, summing to the 100 bps a trader pays with nothing added on top. No ERC-8004 agent bound (bindAgent false, agentId 0).
